fatal_errors: The proposed ZrC addition does not reconstruct the target intervention, which was optimization of low-temperature HVAF-i7 deposition of FeCoNiCrAl to produce a dense, minimally oxidized bond coat.
The cited evidence concerns aqueous NaCl corrosion, not high-temperature oxidation, thermally grown oxide formation, or thermal-cycle durability; it therefore does not support the claimed mechanism.
The proposed CrMnFeCoNi-type baseline lacks Al and is not shown to form the protective alumina TGO required of the target bond-coat system.
The proposed 500–900 °C thermal-cycling regime does not match the demonstrated 1000–1150 °C isothermal oxidation regime.
explanation: The response addresses the broad goal of improving an HEA bond coat and offers a reasonably controlled falsification experiment, but it is scientifically and evidentially remote from the hidden target. The target relies on medium-setting HVAF-i7 processing to obtain 0.2% porosity, suppress deposition oxidation and oxygen ingress, retain the BCC FeCoNiCrAl phase, and form a thin continuous alumina TGO. The generated hypothesis instead substitutes a ZrC-reinforced Cantor-type alloy and invokes speculative oxygen-barrier and grain-pinning effects. Its only evidence establishes improved room-temperature saline corrosion, which cannot validate high-temperature oxidation or TBC adhesion claims. The untreated control and caveats about excess ZrC are useful, and the paired cycling experiment could distinguish performance, although its falsification rule should specify quantitative endpoints and should not require simultaneous failure of every claimed benefit.
